I'm checking each option for whether it captures the aversive tension of a genuine decision conflict, versus just describing responsibility or difficulty. The first one seems to lack that tied-to-choice distress, the second one about "can't lift either one" fits since it shows distress from both options being unwanted, and I'm still weighing whether the third is ambiguous enough to exclude.

Continuing through the rest, "impossible tonight" and being worn down qualifies, but general heaviness or back-and-forth without an aversive quality don't. "Hard to breathe thinking about this choice," feeling low turning it over, "too much weight," and "tired down to my bones" all seem to carry that genuine distress, so I'm leaning toward including them alongside the stomach-stone one, while skipping the ones that read as heaviness alone.
